description:
Nyxel nace de la unión de estudiantes de ESPOL con intereses en programación, análisis de datos e IA. 

Creemos que cada integrante aporta una pieza distinta, y que trabajar juntos nos permite resolver problemas complejos con creatividad y método. Desde Guayaquil, Ecuador, buscamos aprovechar los datos abiertos de la NASA para proponer ideas originales, útiles y construidas con rigor técnico.
summary: ORBIS is an interactive 3D globe that helps find places on Earth that resemble the Moon or Mars, including lesser-known sites. We built a web app that shows each place with a similarity score from 0 to 100, calculated from five variables: elevation, slope, roughness, mean temperature and insolation, taken from NASADEM (LP DAAC) and NASA POWER. Depending on the mission to be tested (rover, habitat, solar panels, landing or drilling), each variable carries a different weight and the ranking changes. Users can zoom into a site, and compare the place with its Martian or lunar counterpart on two side-by-side globes. This addresses the challenge by offering a clear, repeatable way to choose analog sites where technology can be tested before it goes to space. It matters because it lowers mission cost and risk and brings NASA data closer to students and the public. The prototype includes four real sites and uses test reference values for Mars and the Moon, which will be replaced with MOLA, LOLA and Diviner data.
details: ORBIS is an interactive 3D globe that helps space agencies find places on Earth that resemble the Moon and Mars, so rovers, habitats, solar panels, landing systems, and drills can be tested before launch. Each site gets a similarity score from 0 to 100, calculated from five variables (elevation, slope, terrain roughness, mean temperature, and solar insolation), with weights that change depending on the mission being tested. Terrain data comes from NASA’s NASADEM/SRTMGL1 (LP DAAC), and climate data from NASA POWER (MERRA-2 and CERES, 2020–2025). We built it as a static web app using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Globe.gl on Three.js, Python scripts for terrain and climate processing, and Esri satellite imagery plus NASA texture maps, and we published it on GitHub Pages, so it runs in any browser with nothing to install. Its creativity lies in letting users compare an Earth site and its Moon or Mars counterpart side by side on two globes, and in a 20 × 20 km “analyzed zone” that shows exactly which parameters were measured and where. Our team considered mission-specific needs, simple Spanish-language interface design, and honest limits: our Moon and Mars reference values are still placeholders pending MOLA, LOLA, and Diviner data, and terrain values are averages of 1° × 1° tiles. We hope ORBIS makes analog-site selection faster, more transparent, and accessible to students and researchers, including those in Ecuador.
